Today: 2026-06-15
ADR-19 Tamarind: what to do with the Glimmer media-store migration after the cloud-contract review. Project: Tamarind (moving the Glimmer photo-sharing backend from self-hosted MongoDB and Ceph to managed cloud services). Other Glimmer architecture records are referenced at the end. Date: 15 June 2026. Status of this record: decision deferred. Decider: Ayodele Martins (CTO). Prepared by: Rhea Kapoor, Stefan Lund.

Context
Tamarind was started in February to migrate 1.8 petabytes of user photos from our Ceph cluster to cloud object storage and the metadata from self-hosted MongoDB to a managed document database, finishing by October 31, when the hardware lease on the Ceph cluster ends. By June the metadata migration tooling was written and tested on a 5 percent shard, and the dual-write path for new uploads was in staging.

In May, finance and procurement reviewed the cloud contract renewal. The cloud provider's new pricing raises egress and request charges for workloads like ours by about 40 percent. At the same time, the Ceph hardware vendor offered to extend the lease on the existing cluster for three years at 55 percent of the original monthly price, including a refresh of the oldest nodes.

Options considered
1. Continue Tamarind on the new cloud pricing.
2. Continue Tamarind but move to a different cloud provider, which means re-doing the tooling and the security review.
3. Accept the lease extension and keep photos and metadata on our own infrastructure.

Analysis
Over three years, option 1 costs 2.6 times as much as option 3. Option 2 is cheaper than option 1, but it restarts the security review and the tooling work, and would still cost about 1.7 times option 3. Operating our own cluster remains a burden for the four-person storage team, but the lease refresh removes the failing nodes that started this whole discussion.

Decision
On June 10 the CTO decided that Tamarind cannot continue until the board's finance committee chooses between option 1 and option 3, because both commit the company to multi-year spending above the CTO's approval limit. The committee has not put the item on an agenda yet. Until it decides, no photos or metadata may be moved, the dual-write path stays in staging but is not switched on in production, and the cloud buckets for the pilot shard are frozen as they are. Rhea and Stefan are helping the storage team with routine work while the decision is pending; the Ceph vendor has agreed to hold its lease offer open until the committee has decided.

Consequences
- Ceph remains the photo store until the committee decides; the storage team will keep capacity plans for both outcomes.
- The metadata migration tooling stays in the repository unchanged.
- The security review for the cloud storage design, which was 80 percent done, stays open where it stopped.

Other records
- ADR-16, which chose the image-resizing library, is unaffected.
- ADR-17 proposed moving video transcoding to a cloud service; it is still under discussion and is independent of this record.
- ADR-18 introduced the dual-write pattern for uploads; it stays in force.
- The Glimmer web-app redesign is running two weeks behind its own plan for unrelated reasons.

Communication
The decision was announced at the engineering all-hands on June 11. Questions go to the #storage channel or to Rhea directly.

今天：2026-10-21
ADR-007：Orchid 會員點數上鏈方案的去留
所屬專案：Orchid（以聯盟鏈發行跨品牌會員點數，2026/03 啟動）
撰寫：架構師 Dennis 葉　決策會議：2026-10-19 產品暨架構聯席會議　決策狀態：Accepted

背景
Orchid 的目標，是讓集團旗下 5 個品牌的會員點數以聯盟鏈（Hyperledger Fabric）記帳，點數可以跨品牌互換，並開放外部合作商家加入，原訂 2027/01 上線第一階段。截至 9 月，鏈上記帳與 3 個品牌的錢包整合已完成，測試環境的交易吞吐達 800 TPS。

觸發事件
9 月主管機關發布新的函釋：可跨品牌、跨商家流通，且能兌換現金等值商品的點數，認定為類似儲值支付工具，發行者須申請電子支付執照並提撥履約保證。法遵處評估，集團申請執照至少要 18 個月，履約保證需凍結約 NT$3 億。

選項
1. 取得電子支付執照後再上線：時程與資金成本都無法接受。
2. 縮小為單一品牌內使用：失去跨品牌互換的核心價值，而且單一品牌的點數系統早已存在，不需要區塊鏈。
3. 終止 Orchid。

決策
聯席會議 10/19 採用選項 3：Orchid 終止，不再開發，第一階段不上線，跨品牌點數互換的構想一併撤回。鏈上測試網路 11 月底關閉，測試資料依資安規範銷毀。

後果
- 錢包整合程式中的會員身分驗證模組，可以移植到集團的統一會員中心，由會員中心團隊評估。
- Fabric 節點的雲端資源於 11/30 前釋放，每月約省 NT$26 萬。
- Orchid 團隊 6 人中，4 人轉到統一會員中心專案，2 人轉到資料平台。

附註
本次聯席會議也核准了「統一會員中心 2.0」的預算；該案是獨立專案，時程不受本 ADR 影響。

Today: 2026-05-14
Cedar Valley Community Food Bank - Board of Directors, minutes of the regular meeting on 12 May 2026. The project these minutes record a decision on is the Mobile Pantry van programme; the board also heard reports on other programmes.

Present: Helen Marsh (chair), Robert Quinlan (treasurer), Amara Nwachukwu, Diego Salazar, Patricia Holm. Staff: executive director Sandra Lowell; programmes manager Jamal Wright.

1. Approval of the April minutes - approved unanimously.

2. Treasurer's report
Robert reported that individual donations are 8 percent above last year, but corporate giving fell sharply after two local employers closed their regional offices. Operating reserves stand at 4.2 months of expenses, below the board's 6-month policy.

3. Mobile Pantry van programme
Background: the programme was approved in October 2025 to buy a refrigerated van and run weekly distribution stops in five rural townships without a grocery store, starting in July 2026. It depended on a three-year grant from the Halvern Family Trust covering the van and a driver's salary. Jamal reported that the trust notified us on May 4 that, because of its own investment losses, it is withdrawing all new grant commitments, including ours. Staff looked for replacement funding for three weeks without success, and the county's rural-transport fund will not open again until 2028. After discussion, Diego moved that the Mobile Pantry van programme be discontinued, the deposit on the van be recovered under the dealer's cancellation terms, and the five township partners be informed that the distribution stops will not start. The motion passed 5-0. Sandra will write to each township partner this week and will offer them places in the existing partner-agency network so their residents can still be referred.

4. Warehouse cooler expansion
The contractor is about three weeks behind because the compressor units were back-ordered; completion is now expected in late July. Cold storage capacity during June will be tight, and Jamal will schedule produce deliveries accordingly.

5. Weekend backpack programme for schools
Running in 14 schools. The school district asked whether we could add three more in the autumn; staff will cost it for the June meeting.

6. Volunteer management software
Waiting on the vendor to finish the data import from our old spreadsheets; volunteers cannot be scheduled in the new system until it is done, so the old sign-up sheets stay in use.

7. Annual fundraising gala
Set for September 19 at the Riverside Hall. Patricia reported that 11 of 20 sponsor tables are sold.

8. Executive director's report
Sandra noted that pounds distributed in April were up 12 percent year on year, driven by higher demand from working families. Two long-serving volunteers will be honoured at the June meeting.

9. Other business
The board discussed the reserves shortfall and asked the treasurer to bring a two-year plan to restore the 6-month reserve.

Adjourned at 8:42 pm. Next meeting: 9 June 2026. Minutes recorded by Amara Nwachukwu, approved by the chair on 14 May.
